architecture_delta.authority: UnifiedDB remains canonical truth; ClayGraph remains derived relevance; packet selection never grants effect authority; Hyperposition alternatives remain explicit
architecture_delta.policy: adaptive STANDING/HYBRID/LAZY materialization based on observed read savings vs update+storage cost

counterhypothesis: For cold or high-update contexts, standing materialization can cost more than lazy query-time derivation; some query shapes cannot be maintained at constant update cost.
hypothesis: Standing provenance-bound possibility packets can preserve exact structured selection while moving expensive relational/graph composition off the hot cognitive path.
limitations: single local KVM host for aggregate runs
no real Frank v0.1 interaction replay yet
no Hostinger self-hosted runner evidence yet at receipt creation time

methods.ground_truth: exact relational derivation using identical deterministic selector semantics
methods.packet_path: canonical context signature -> v_current_possibility_packets -> pre-ranked top-3 packet
methods.query_contexts_per_run: 102-115 valid goal/constraint signatures depending on seed
methods.text_baseline: SQLite FTS5 rule/document retrieval followed by first valid resource binding; baseline is intentionally text-retrieval, not a claim about all databases
methods.update_test: mutate one high-fanout capability reliability, invalidate dependency closure, retire affected candidate versions, regenerate affected resource candidates, recompile affected signatures, compare selection to independent full rebuild

negative_results: A separate top-k frontier table followed by a hot-path join was semantically correct but slower than direct prepared-index lookup on the first prototype; it was rejected.
Packet JSON parsing adds a small overhead relative to direct prepared-row lookup, but remains far below query-time relational derivation and reduces the model-facing payload to top-3.
promotion_gate: Do not promote from synthetic evidence. Next gate requires Ubuntu self-hosted runner parity, concurrent epoch/invalidation tests, recovery/rebuild tests, and replay on real project/Frank semantic workloads.
